passages.original: fecerunt tamen tres gravissimi scriptores, Basilius, Gregorius Nazianzenus, et Hieronymus, cu- lus sunt haec verba de Papia : Hic dicitur mille an- norum Judaicam edidisseδευτέρωσα, quem secuti sunt Irenoeus et Apollinarius, qui post resurrectionem aiunt in carne cum sanctis Dominum reqnaturum (De Script. Eccl. c. 28). Immo cum adversus Irenaeum, implica- tum ad hunc errorem, Dionysius Alexandrinus scri- psisset, testatur Hieronymus (Prooem. ad. c.lxvIsa.) ouobus voluminibus respondisse Apollinarium.
passages.english: Three very weighty writers, however, did [mention it]: Basil, Gregory of Nazianzus, and Jerome, whose words about Papias are these: "He is said to have put forth the Jewish *deuterōsis* [secondary tradition] of a thousand years, and he was followed by Irenaeus and Apollinarius, who say that after the resurrection the Lord will reign in the flesh with the saints" (On Ecclesiastical Writers, ch. 28). Indeed, when Dionysius of Alexandria had written against Irenaeus, who was entangled in this error, Jerome testifies (Preface to [Book 18 of the Commentary on] Isaiah) that Apollinarius replied in two volumes.
passages.notes: Scanning errors silently corrected: 'cu- lus' (cuius), 'an- norum', 'reqnaturum' (regnaturum), 'scri- psisset', 'ouobus' (duobus). The Greek δευτέρωσα is evidently δευτέρωσιν, a term for Jewish secondary (rabbinic) tradition, here applied to millenarian teaching. The reference 'Prooem. ad. c.lxvIsa.' is garbled; it seems to point to Jerome's preface to the book of his Isaiah commentary that deals with ch. 66 or nearby (usually Book 18), but the exact reference is uncertain. The opening 'fecerunt' continues the preceding context ('made mention'), hence the bracketed supplement.
